messages.subject: Re: [unmarked] NaNs
parts:
hi Sharon,
 Can you send an example of the output?
 Its possible the NaN's are just optimization warnings and not errors. This would be common in complex models.
 Also, I don't understand when you say you have covariates for abundance, recruitment, survival and detectability. You must be using the pcountOPEN function and not pcount, right?
 If you have sparse data its possible that some of the parameters are weakly or not identifiable at all. I suggest starting with the simplest model and building it up by adding covariates one-at-a-time.
regards
andy


On Thu, Jul 26, 2012 at 5:12 PM, Sharon <sharo...@gmail.com> wrote:
Hello,
 
I am trying to better understand the variety of reasons that NaN's arise, based on my own observations in running pcount models.
 
I have covariates for abundance, recruitement, apparent survival, and detectability. What seems to be happening is that when I get a “model did not converge” error and then I re-run using start values…the model ends up converging and there are no more NaN errors. In contrast, when I get the NaN’s but no “model did not converge” error and I try using start values….the NaN’s do **not** go away.
 
So it sounds like one gets NaN's for more than just model non-convergence.
 
Also, I am wondering how I can get NaN errors for a model that is MORE parsimonious than another, where the two only differ by one covariate. Specifically, I have two models that only differ in the detectability covariates (specifically, Model 1 has 3 covariates and Model 2 has 4). For Model 2 I don't get any NaN's, but for Model 1 in Apparent Survival I get two NaN for 2 of the parameters.
 
Thank you!
 
Sharon
